problem:
Given that the differential equation 

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-5y=-4\operatorname{cos}⁡x
$$

has the complementary solution ${y}_{c}(x)=A{e}^{5x}$, find the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x)$ to this equation.

${y}_{p}(x)=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
To find the general solution of an inhomogeneous first-order linear equation with constant coefficients on the left-hand side, we must find the sum of the complementary and particular solutions.

The right-hand side of the inhomogeneous equation is $-4\operatorname{cos}⁡x.$ So, we assume the particular solution to be 

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡x+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡x.
$$

where $\alpha $ and $\beta $ are constants to be determined. 

Calculating the first derivative of ${y}_{p}$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}x}=-\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡x+\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡x.
$$

To find the values of $\alpha $ and $\beta ,$ we substitute ${y}_{p}$ and ${y}_{p}^{′}$ into the differential equation:

$$
(-\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡x+\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡x)-5(\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡x+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡x)=-4\operatorname{cos}⁡x.
$$

Grouping the terms on the left-hand side gives

$$
(\beta -5\alpha )\operatorname{cos}⁡x+(-\alpha -5\beta )\operatorname{sin}⁡x=-4\operatorname{cos}⁡x.
$$

Equating the coefficients, we get the following system of equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}\beta -5\alpha =-4\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡x) \\ -\alpha -5\beta =0\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system gives $\alpha =\frac{10}{13},$ $\beta =-\frac{2}{13}.$

Therefore, the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x)$ is

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=\frac{10}{13}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)-\frac{2}{13}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x).
$$
